- **The change:** `_entry_statements`' verbless in-label branch now calls a new `_clause_heads(line)` (`src/gov/store/loader.py`). It applies rules (1)–(4):
  - (1) the value ends at ` · ` and at a list-item line break at any indentation (`_LIST_ITEM`: `\n[ \t]*(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])[ \t]`);
  - (2) it splits into clauses at each `;` outside parentheses;
  - (3) a clause's head is its text before its first `:` outside parentheses, or the whole clause when it has none;
  - (4) the changers are the head's ids outside parentheses.
- **Unchanged:** each head still gives amend, or supersede for **Superseded by:**. Labels with a verb, the out-labels, **Superseded:**, free text and the change log are untouched.
- **The brief's question, whether the cut should be shared:** no. If rule (1)'s cut applied to the out-labels, it would drop real targets from 10 **Changes:** labels on this register: DEC-889, 892, 896, 899, 904, 906, 922, 923, 924 and 925. Those sub-items deliberately list the decisions changed. It would change no verb in-label. So the cut stays in the verbless branch only.

**risks:**
- A `(` that is never closed hides the rest of the value's ids. No such case on this register; there's a unit case for it.

**lessons:** In this repo, `-k "not real…"` isn't what drops parametrised rows; conftest's opt-in representative rule is. Use `--optin=lifted,breadth` to see every row.
